item.description: Resolving to take better care of your skin is a great place to start improving your health. Here are three steps to help lower skin cancer risk.

item.title: Your January Update: Winter Skin Health & You - The Skin Cancer Foundation
item.description: As daylight hours steadily increase, you have more time to get outside to walk, run, hike and participate in winter sports. We’re here to remind you to practice sun safety, even when it’s cold outside. No matter the season, UV radiation can be sneaky. It reaches you at home, in your car and outside, even when it’s snowing.

item.title: Skin Cancer Does Not Discriminate — Even Pro Athletes Get It - The Skin Cancer Foundation
item.description: Jake Schweitzer wants people to know: Skin cancer is serious and can happen to anyone, even pro athletes. Jake is working with The Skin Cancer Foundation to raise awareness about skin cancer prevention.

item.title: Your February Update: The Truth About Skin Cancer - The Skin Cancer Foundation
item.description: While skin cancer rates steadily rise, skin cancer myths and misinformation are running rampant online, including unsafe tanning trends, untrue sunscreen claims and dangerous skin health misconceptions.

item.title: 2025 in Review: Updated Standards and a New Destination Healthy Skin RV - The Skin Cancer Foundation
item.description: In 2025, The Skin Cancer Foundation expanded programs, updated standards and worked tirelessly to educate the public about skin cancer and the importance of sun protection and early detection.
